mainText:
A wintry blast is bringing snow, frost and rain across the country, with temperatures forecast to fall as low as minus nine in the South Island tonight.

New Zealand.

A wintry blast has brought snow, gale force winds and rain across the North Island, with road snowfall warnings in place nationwide and temperatures forecast to drop to minus nine in parts of the South Island overnight.

A knife attack in Hamilton has put four people in hospital. A twenty three year old man is in police custody. Separately, police in Waikato are examining a burning car found on a rural road near Waitomo, with a body inside. The death is being treated as unexplained.

A young adult has died of meningococcal disease in Waikato. Health New Zealand is urging people to learn the symptoms and get vaccinated, warning the disease can progress within hours.

In Auckland, a large fire tore through Botany Town Centre, sending thick black smoke over the cinema at its peak. Firefighters have brought the blaze under control.

In the Bay of Plenty, the government has extended the public submission window for its inquiry into the January landslides that killed eight people at Mount Maunganui and Pāpāmoa. Western Bay of Plenty District Council also faces a byelection after Alan Kurtovich quit over the district's Māori wards decision, a vote he says was worth the cost to his position.

National's leadership fallout continues. Chris Penk has confirmed he is quitting Parliament after nine years, following last week's failed challenge to Christopher Luxon. ACT's David Seymour has called the episode a shit show. Luxon is pressing on with campaigning in the South Island, telling Nelson voters he is focused on the party's regional plans with under three months until the election.

World.

Twelve people have been killed and dozens seriously injured after a Polish tourist bus veered off a motorway and overturned in Hungary early on Sunday morning. Hungarian authorities say the driver may have fallen asleep at the wheel.

A magnitude seven point seven earthquake in eastern Indonesia has killed at least fifty three people, with rescue teams recovering four more bodies on Sunday. Patients are being treated in tents after the quake damaged a hospital, and the toll is expected to keep rising as search efforts continue in remote areas.

Ukraine has launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, with Russia saying more than eight hundred drones were shot down and at least seven people killed in strikes on Moscow and Kyiv. Fires broke out across the Ukrainian capital overnight.

A wildfire in Belgium has more than doubled in size over three days, burning over twenty seven square kilometres of nature reserve and forcing hundreds to evacuate as it spreads toward the German border. It is being described as one of the country's worst wildfires on record.

Technology.

Wall Street banks have committed five hundred billion US dollars to Nvidia to fund new data centres for artificial intelligence processing, extending a surge in AI infrastructure spending. The money will build facilities to house and cool the computer chips that process AI workloads, as demand for computing capacity continues to outstrip supply.

Amazon's Twitch platform is facing backlash after confirming it is using streamers' content to train generative AI under an opt out system, meaning users are included unless they actively withdraw. Separately, tech bosses including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg continue to publish lengthy public manifestos on AI, a trend commentators say reflects growing competition to shape the public narrative around the technology.

Sport.

League. NRL. The Warriors beat the Broncos at Suncorp Stadium last weekend, a result that has already aired. New analysis says halfback Luke Metcalf may not play again this year after hobbling off with a hamstring injury. In the NRLW, the Kiwi Ferns' Warriors lost thirty to twenty two to the Wests Tigers, with Jesse McGregor dominating for the Tigers. Winger Stacey Waaka, the sevens convert, continues to impress at centre, setting up tries for teammates.

Rugby. Canterbury held out Bay of Plenty thirty three to twenty eight at Te Kaha Stadium to retain the Ranfurly Shield, a result that has already aired. Bay of Plenty led for long periods before Canterbury's defence closed out the win.

Swimming. Erika Fairweather won a second bronze medal at the Pan Pacific Championships in California, finishing behind Australian gold medallist Lani Pallister and American Katie Ledecky. That result has already aired but underlines a strong meet for the New Zealand team.

Tennis. New Zealand number one Lulu Sun is taking a break from the tour. She says the physical and mental demands of playing at the top level have become relentless. No return date has been set.

Basketball. New Zealand coach Tab Baldwin has been perpetually banned from university sport in the Philippines, following player deaths linked to his programme. The University Athletic Association of the Philippines says the sanction is final and cannot be appealed.

Coming up. Parliament sits again this week as National's campaign resumes. The Western Bay of Plenty byelection continues. Watch for developments in the Waitomo car death investigation and further aftershocks from the Indonesia earthquake.

End of flash.
